module purpose: neorv32_sysinfo assembles four 32-bit information words: word 0 is reset-initialized from a constant and can be overwritten by a qualified bus write, while words 1 to 3 are derived from generic-controlled constant expressions. It buffers request strobe and address bits, then returns the selected word on the bus response with an acknowledge and a tied-low error.

use-case flows.value: 32-bit system-information word 0 written from bus_req_i.data on a qualified write to word address 0
build-time system configuration descriptor words 1 to 3 derived from generic-controlled constants and feature-enable bits
selected system-information word returned using buffered address and buffered request strobe
system-information word 0 reset to the CLOCK_FREQUENCY constant and response buffers cleared while rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Runtime-updatable system-information word 0, reset-loaded from CLOCK_FREQUENCY
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module stores this word in sysinfo: the reset arm assigns `std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(CLOCK_FREQUENCY, 32))` at line 92 when `rstn_i = '0'` (line 91), and the clocked write at line 95 copies `bus_req_i.data` when `bus_req_i.stb`, `bus_req_i.rw` and `bus_req_i.addr(3 downto 2) = "00"` hold (line 94). The held value is then read out through `bus_rsp_o.data <= sysinfo(...)` at line 168. Integrity is established because the configure and read-out flows depend on this word matching either the reset-loaded constant or the last accepted write; availability is also established because the register holds the value between writes. The bus request/response ports are transport records and are therefore not reported as structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Build-time system configuration descriptor words 1 to 3
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes these descriptor words directly in sysinfo from constant and generic-controlled expressions: sysinfo(1) fields at lines 102-105, sysinfo(2) feature bits at lines 109-140, and sysinfo(3) cache-related fields at lines 144-150. Line 168 returns the selected sysinfo word on the response data path. Integrity is established because the read-out flow depends on delivering exactly these defined descriptor values to the consumer; availability is also established because these combinational values are present whenever selected. The map records these assignments only under `constant_drivers` for sysinfo, so there is no receiving relationship edge to cite for the compute role.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered response word index deciding which system-information word is returned
conceptual assets.reasoning: The access buffer stores the requested word index in `buf_adr`: it is reset to `00` at line 158, and on a rising clock edge it captures `bus_req_i.addr(3 downto 2)` when `bus_req_i.stb = '1'` at lines 161-162. Line 168 then uses `sysinfo(to_integer(unsigned(buf_adr)))` to choose the response data word. Integrity is established because the read-out flow depends on returning the addressed word; availability is also established because the selector is held in the register until the response is formed.

conceptual assets.concept: Buffered acknowledge/data-valid state for the bus response
conceptual assets.reasoning: `buf_ack` is the stored response-valid/acknowledge state: it is reset to `'0'` at line 157, loaded from `bus_req_i.stb` at line 160, gates the response data at line 168, and is copied to `bus_rsp_o.ack` at line 169. Integrity is established because both handshake correctness and response-data qualification depend on this captured bit; availability is also established because the module produces and holds the acknowledge state from the captured strobe.
